body:
A start that fails because of node state costs a full boot cycle before it says why. Three ways this happens:

- a worker is missing the image (`cluster start --apply` doesn't distribute it, so the start fails);
- a node's checkout is behind the head (any merge on the head blocks every start until the nodes are synced again);
- the profile isn't in any commit, so it only exists on the host that wrote it.

All three refusals are correct, but each one shows up late. This change makes `cluster sync` the single command that brings every node in line. It also makes the `cluster start` plan list every problem `--apply` would stop on, along with the command that fixes it.

## Changes

- **`cluster sync --apply` copies the image.** As its last step, sync copies the image the profile names from the head to every node whose image layers differ (the existing `docker save | ssh docker load` path). The plan without `--apply` lists those nodes. If the head lacks the right build, sync only warns, because a lab image step may build after the sync. If the checkout isn't at the deployed commit, sync copies nothing and says so.
- **Uncommitted profiles are refused before any checkout.** If a node lacks the profile and the deployed commit doesn't include it (for example an ignored `*.local.json`), sync stops before fetching and says to commit and publish the profile.
- **The `cluster start` plan runs the full preflight.** It runs the same read-only checks as `--apply`, both on this host and on every node, and prints `preflight: clean` or every finding. Findings that sync repairs are marked as drift: a node checkout behind the head, a missing committed profile, or a worker image that's missing or stale. Drift findings end with:
  ```
  fix: bin/spark --cluster-config <profile> cluster sync --apply gives every node this commit and its image
  ```
  If the head itself lacks the right image, the finding names `build image --apply` instead. `--apply` still refuses and changes nothing on the nodes; it now prints the same fix line.
- **`build distribute` shares the image helpers** with sync. It now refuses a host build whose labels don't match the profile.

Docs updated: `docs/setup.md`, `docs/doctor.md`, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`.

## Behaviour to note

- Lab's `sync_checkouts()` runs `cluster sync --apply` with the production profile. That sync will now also copy the production image to any node whose layers differ, which can add a few minutes the first time.
- Sync still never copies an ignored cluster profile. Only the site's node map and `site.json` are copied.

## Verification

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`: 635 tests OK. New tests cover the plan's preflight and fix line, drift classification on the head and on workers, image copy and skip, failed loads, the uncommitted-profile refusal, local image label checks, and `build distribute`.
- `bin/spark doctor` exits 0; `git diff --check` is clean; `scripts/render_docs.py --check` is clean.
- Not yet run against the cluster: the image copy and the node preflight were exercised only through unit tests.
title: cluster: sync copies the profile's image, and the start plan runs the full preflight
